An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy range, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported - namely, a right ascension-based dipolar modulation. To further investigate, we divided the most energetic group into three segments, and discovered that this anisotropy becomes increasingly pronounced with rising energy levels above 4 EeV, exhibiting an energy-dependent pattern that adheres to a power law with an index of 0.79 ± 0.19. We also discovered that the orientation of these anisotropy patterns supports their extragalactic origins, across all energy levels examined. Furthermore, an investigation of quadrupolar components revealed that they lacked sufficient statistical significance. We interpret our findings within the context of theoretical models proposing the distribution of extremely energetic cosmic sources and cosmic magnetic field dynamics.

The ATLAS detector at the LHC gathered p+Pb data with a centre of mass energy of 5.02 TeV and 25 nanobarns of integrated luminosity, enabling a comparison with interpolated pp measurements at 2.76 and 7 TeV. Owing to its sophisticated design and reliability, the ATLAS detector successfully collected a comprehensive dataset during heavy ion and proton-proton runs. As a result, it facilitated precise measurements of the nuclear modification factor, obtained by dividing charged particle yields from heavy ion collisions by their proton-proton counterparts in various centrality ranges and rapidity intervals. Furthermore, this analysis reveals a notable variation in the nuclear modification factor with transverse momentum, showing a more pronounced trend in more peripheral collisions.

The paper provides an in-depth analysis of a class of noncommutative quantum mechanical systems, associated with Lie algebras. Initially, it offers nontrivial commutation relations between position and momentum operators, then examines their impact on the structure of phase space. Furthermore, it investigates noncommutative parameters on both dynamic and algebraic properties of quantum mechanical systems, utilizing a linear transformation approach. Notably, it derives a connection between noncommutative and commutative parameters, offering practical applications to specific Lie algebras.

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training deep learning models to analyze digitized tissue samples, specifically in a classification application involving the detection of tumor cells within whole-slide images. By simulating a FL environment with a large, diverse dataset of cancer images from various sources, we compared the results of training models using both a federated approach and a centralized approach. Our findings indicate that federated learning can produce models with similar accuracy to those trained with centralized data, while avoiding the need to collect extensive training datasets at a single location. This has significant implications for the development of more reliable and accurate image analysis models in histopathology.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving a data rate of 40Gb/s and a distance of 3,500 meters in a real-world underwater environment. The system overcomes the impact of burst errors caused by water bubbles using a decision feedback equalizer, but this leads to symbol interference and eventual error propagation. A new algorithm, the Burst-Error Suppression (BES) algorithm, is introduced to prevent the spread of errors, and its performance is tested under various conditions of burst length and magnitude. Furthermore, an improved version of the algorithm, the Bes' (BES Prime) algorithm, proposes the use of probabilistic methods to enhance the decision feedback equalizer's performance and restore its original capacity to operate over long distances with bubble impairments.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) hold great promise for handling time-series data. TCNs leverage a technique called time-dilated convolution that poses an optimization challenge which typically demands significant experimentation. We've developed a technique to automate the dilation optimization process by casting it as a weight-pruning operation along the time axis. Our method learns dilation factors concurrently with weights during training and achieves notable gains in model compactness and inference efficiency without compromising accuracy. It produces a range of highly optimal TCN variants from a single starting model, surpassing the performance of custom-designed networks in both efficiency and accuracy.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

The CMS collaboration has analyzed data from Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 5.02 TeV, specifically examining v{n}hphi{n} correlations for various n (ranging from 2 to 7) between pairs of charged hadrons with transverse momenta greater than 2.5 TeV, and has found that the fluctuations in flow angles are more pronounced at higher values of n. Moreover, the average elliptic flow differences, <v2hphi2)> - v2, exhibit a decrease with increasing transverse momentum. It has been noted that one-dimensional flow dominates at large values of p_T and that fluctuations in flow angles become less pronounced as n increases. Furthermore, it is suggested that quark-gluon plasma may influence these fluctuations in flow angles.

The unified correspondence theory leverages the algebraic and order theoretic underpinnings of Sahlqvist correspondence to offer versatile tools for correspondence and canonicity across diverse semantic frameworks and signatures. These tools, specifically tailored to logics whose semantics rely on normal lattice expansions (DLEs), enable computation of first-order correspondents for inductive formulas using the algorithm ALBA. Conversely, our proposed method effectively employs ALBA's rules and algebraic language to reverse its computations in the DLE setting, thereby allowing the derivation of an inductive formula from its first-order correspondent.

We examine relationships between functional dependencies and data, considering dependencies as constraints on tables that may contain missing values. This approach handles cases where dependencies are violated due to incomplete data. We define two semantics for handling partial data: one that considers all possible completions of incomplete tables. A more innovative approach is developed for handling incomplete tables that specify data and dependencies. We prove a characterisation of which sets of dependencies can be applied to tables. A significant challenge arises from the fact that data may be inconsistent with functional dependencies in partially defined tables, in contrast to the situation in completely defined databases. We address this challenge by identifying characterizations of functional dependencies over incomplete tables that are stable under certain operations.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research indicates that a score-driven approach is particularly effective in capturing the evolution of time-varying parameters and allows for modeling complex dynamics and shifts within such data sets. Furthermore, we have analyzed the theoretical characteristics of the TV-PARX model, demonstrating under mild conditions that maximum likelihood estimation yields reliable and normally-distributed estimates of model parameters. To evaluate the TV-PARX model's performance and forecasting capabilities in real-world scenarios, we conducted a series of Monte Carlo simulations. Additionally, we have applied the time-varying specification of the TV-PARX model to empirical data sets, analyzing new daily COVID-19 cases in Italy and corporate defaults in the US.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation,
with the aim of repeating tasks on new object instances from the same category
after witnessing a single demonstration. To achieve this, we use optimization
to locate the pose whose descriptor corresponds to that in the demonstration. NDFs
are efficiently trained without expert input, using a self-supervised 3D
auto-encoder, and exhibit robust performance across 6-DoF rotations and translations.
In experiments, NDFs master tasks from just a handful (5-10) demonstrations,
in both simulation and with a physical robot. Results show our method excels at
generalizing over different object instances and poses, surpassing a comparison
method relying on 2D descriptors. The NDF project is hosted at https://yilundu.github.io/ndf/.

The SiD Detector is one of the two validated detector designs for the future ILC, specifically tailored to meet precision demands for the Higgs boson and other research areas while maintaining an adaptable sensitivity to diverse potential discoveries. The SiD's robust silicon vertex and tracking system, complemented by its high central magnetic field, ensures precise momentum measurement. The detector's finely granulated calorimeter system, designed for particle flow analysis, delivers accurate energy resolution across a wide energy range. Given the approaching construction timeline for the ILC, the time has come to reassess the design choices made during the design phase and incorporate the recent breakthroughs in technology into the review process. This review will discuss R&D prospects and participation opportunities for the SiD's development areas.

We performed the first in-depth analysis of an open cluster located in the Galactic bulge, utilizing a range of observations from the M4 branch of the APOgee Survey. Specifically, we utilized 1D and 5D spectral analyses to determine fundamental properties of the cluster, including its age, metallicity, abundance patterns, velocity vector, and physical characteristics. Our analysis was based on 14 member stars observed with APOgee and supplemented by data from the NEAR survey. Our results indicate that the cluster is situated approximately 4.3 kpc above the Galactic plane, in the outer regions of the bulge. Our 5D spectral analysis revealed that the cluster has a age of 4.8 billion years, a metallicity of [Fe/H] = 0.19, an alpha/Fe ratio of 0.1, an ellipticity of 0.26, and a velocity vector in the l/b/ b direction of 191/-19/119 with a space rotation angle of 21.8 degrees. Our analysis revealed several similarities between the Cluster Tonantzintla 2 and the open cluster M4, suggesting a possible relationship between the two clusters. However, further observations and analyses are necessary to confirm this hypothesis. Our study also contributes to the broader scientific understanding of intermediate-age clusters in the bulge, which are relatively understudied.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has amassed substantial size over recent years, representing an impressive compilation of research and offering a diverse range of opportunities for statistical exploration in the field of theorem proving. Despite the numerous contributions made so far, the ever-expanding nature of the archive still poses certain challenges: locating specific content has become increasingly difficult, making it essential to prioritize reuse and clarity of comprehension. This thesis proposal outlines my research objectives, which focus on these concerns, as well as initial findings, which reveal that the Isabelle Archive exhibits characteristics typical of scale-free networks, as evidenced by the distribution of node in-degrees in its dependency graph.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.589 for $N=6$ and $N=4$ respectively. Alternatively, we have found $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be around 1.583 for the 2D Ising model.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the Z2 synchronization problem and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. Additionally, our inequality led to a confirmation of a previous conjecture regarding the efficiency of a sampling algorithm in the "easy" regime of these models.

Modern metasurfaces, at the intersection of advanced technology and science,  
constitute an intricate field, involving electromagnetic systems characterized by  
thin, expansive, and minutely featured particles that can also vary spatially,  
temporally, and linearly.  To tackle this intricacy, researchers need to employ a  
unified approach, integrating theoretical design and analysis methods, supported  
by an established framework.  Recent breakthroughs, facilitated by Generalized  
Sheet Transition Conditions in combination with surface susceptibilities,  
now enable designers to develop intricate metasurfaces, addressing longstanding  
challenges.  This paper delves into computational modeling of these complex  
structures through GSTC-susceptibility methodology and underscores its critical  
importance in the holistic design of metasurfaces, reviewing the evolution of  
recent frequency and time-domain computational methods.

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth vector fields with a full set of nearby first integrals, especially those at nondegenerate singular points. This theoretical validation relies heavily on key concepts, including the formal orbital linearization theorem for formally integrable vector fields, the application of the blowing-up technique, and the application of the Sternberg-Chen theorem regarding formally equivalent smooth hyperbolic vector fields.

This report outlines a deep learning approach known as the Electron Correlation
Potential Neural Network (eCPNN), which can learn simplified potential functions
that accurately capture the intricate instantaneous relationships among electrons
within complex atomic systems. Trained in an unsupervised manner with constrained
data derived from Full Configuration Interaction one-electron density functions, the
eCPNN model effectively predicts total atomic energies with remarkable precision.

We have serendipitously identified a massive arc-like structure, dubbed a Giant Arc, which lies at a redshift of approximately 0.8. Spanning nearly 1 billion light-years, this feature exhibits remarkable symmetry when viewed from space. It was discovered through a novel approach using intervening magnesium-absorbing systems in the light from background quasars. Our analysis leverages a range of techniques, including a "likelihood map" method, to establish its statistical significance and overcome challenges posed by the uneven distribution of galaxies across the universe. Furthermore, we explore whether the Giant Arc exhibits any alignment with the large-scale cosmic web, finding some evidence to support this theory while acknowledging limitations due to sample size.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical astrophysics, achieving a precision of 0.01 for measuring the aerosol depth has been challenging. By taking wide-field photometry over a broad altitude range, the aerosol depth can be determined quickly, regardless of the system's absolute calibration, and even provides calibration as a by-product. Our team used extensive data from the FRAM telescope at the Pierre Auger Observatory and a similar telescope at the Cherenkov Telescope Array site to improve the precision of this technique to a precision of possibly 0.01. To accomplish this, we conducted precise laboratory measurements of the system's response to varying light intensities and spectra to counter the limitations of non-linear CCD detectors under observation conditions.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) has gained significant interest. Literature can be broadly categorized into two main areas based on whether intermediate cues are employed: direct methods and two-stage pipelines. In the latter category, CNN regresses intermediate cues such as object coordinates or virtual control points instead of pose parameters. Lately, direct methods have outperformed two-stage pipelines due to mitigating source of error accumulation. Nevertheless, direct approaches still struggle with ambiguity due to their tendency to compress data onto a 2D regression map, thereby hindering their effectiveness in pose estimation tasks, particularly in scenarios involving objects with high symmetry. To overcome this limitation, we introduce an innovative strategy that integrates projection grouping and direct learning via a correspondence loss function. As a result, our proposed framework achieves precise regression of both discrete control points and pose parameters by directly learning the mapping between object coordinate patterns and control point patterns. We introduce the DeepHierarchical object pose regression network (DeepHMap++), which is composed of two interconnected CNN branches that share lower-level features. Experimental results on the YCB-Video dataset demonstrate the superiority of DeepHMap++ over state-of-the-art direct and two-stage methods across a wide range of objects.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant expansion in their application across multiple disciplines, due to their ability to model and track discontinuity formation within materials. Bond-based Peridynamics, despite its modeling restrictions, has become a widely-used approach in numerical simulations because of its ease of implementation and intuitive connection to real-world physics. This paper delves into the aspects of bond-based peridynamic models, providing a thorough examination of the theory and its numerical representations. Various bond-based PD integral kernels have been presented along with their distinguishing characteristics, leading to discussions on their implications and common traits. A closer examination was conducted on the role of non-locality in determining motion, the interplay between kernel structure and material non-penetration, as well as the influence of PD kernel non-linearity on predicting fracture development. Finally, an exploration is initiated on adapting BB-PD to model fluids within the context of fading memory materials, suggesting directions for enhanced understanding of fluid dynamics through peridynamics.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed inverse covariance matrix $\Theta$ from
multivariate Gaussian data $\mathcal{X}$, initially introduced by Dempster (1972)
under Covariance Selection. The framework is expanded by generalizing $\mathcal{X}$'s
structure and leveraging the inverse's properties to reduce the problem's
complexity. By incorporating suitable $\Theta$ and $\mathcal{X}$ constraints, Graphical
Lasso serves as a versatile tool for estimating various models, such as Graphical
Lasso with Tree Structure (GTLasso) and Wiedemann Algorithm estimates (WAlgo).
Friedman's (2007) original implementation utilized a generic solver, whereas newer
methods like WAlgo and advanced regularization techniques outperform the baseline
and are beneficial, especially when handling high-dimensional datasets. As these
approaches involve significant computational steps, they can be time-consuming
with large data sets. We propose GGLasso, a library that streamlines solving
structurally constrained inverse covariance estimation problems, with a focus on
related algorithms like WAlgo, enabling both development and replication of
research projects.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized and assessed, focusing on deterministic impulses, drifts, and Brownian motions. By utilizing the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion, recent studies found that the methods' accuracy could be evaluated in terms of the impact of the step size on configurational averaging. Results showed that for harmonic oscillators, some methods yield precise configurational averages, potentially leading to better performance in biomolecular simulations, especially in cases where bond stretches play a crucial role. Furthermore, research found that an optimal method could achieve nearly perfect smallness of impulse contributions, offering efficient and accurate molecular sampling, as demonstrated in benchmark tests comparing potential energy averages with Rao-Blackwell estimates for flexible molecules.

Numerical relativity simulations allow us to study how binary black hole mergers interact with their surroundings. However, these simulations start only shortly before the merger and require predetermined initial conditions to proceed. Therefore, a significant task involves identifying the appropriate configuration for the binary system and its environment at this point in the process. In our research, we've been investigating the behavior of dark matter in the vicinity of black hole binaries of equal mass, discovering a consistent, long-lasting profile that emerges over several orbits. Conversely, systems with greater dark matter mass see overdensities scattered due to the binary's motion. Furthermore, regardless of initial configurations, systems typically converge to the established profile after a certain number of orbits; this convergence often results in the emergence of undesirable, short-lived oscillations. It's also been found that if matter is directly overlaid onto a binary system, without properly considering the potential for matter to influence the binary's motion, this leads to inaccurately calculated orbital paths due to artificial factors, rather than a signature of dark matter at play.

We tackle the persistent issue of exponential stability for a stretched Euler-Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped graph with three equal branches. The model incorporates rotational inertia in all nodes and applies different damping mechanisms to each arm. Our primary goal is to establish the stability of the equation's solution. Leveraging a Lyapunov function, we prove that when the damping coefficients fall within specific ranges, particularly when viscous and thermal dampings maintain the sectorial law, the system's solutions decay at a exponential rate. Additionally, we utilize the semigroup theory to analyze both stability and instability of the system's equations.

Researchers utilized acoustic lenses composed of PMMA to increase the detection area of sensitive devices and improve resolution but discovered these lenses introduced image distortion. This problem was investigated and a new lens material called Stycast 1090SI was proposed as an alternative. The acoustic properties of this novel material were examined alongside PMMA to determine its feasibility. Computational simulations and practical tests using two different materials, PMMA and Stycast 1090SI, showed both materials significantly enhance the detection of sensitive devices. Notably, the Stycast lens exhibited lower levels of distortion compared to the PMMA lens, which could have implications for photoacoustic tomography, particularly in advanced reconstruction algorithms and pattern-reversal techniques. This research demonstrates that the Stycast 1090SI material has excellent acoustic properties and the potential to improve the utilization of large-area detectors in photoacoustic tomography.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

We tackle the issue of non-blind deblurring and demosaicking on noisy raw images using a learning-based approach tailored to handle these images directly, with an innovative new component that simultaneously demosaicks and deblurs them in an interpretable way. To train this model, we utilize real-world camera data transformed into raw images through a realistic process, mimicking real-world camera functions. By doing so, we demonstrate the advantages of our single-stage model over traditional approaches combining demosaicking and deblurring modules, according to objective performance metrics. Additionally, our method is capable of removing a camera's intrinsic blurring effect, which effectively enables deblurring of sharper images from actual pictures.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation in noncommutative spacetime. 
We then successfully transformed the Dirac equation from its linear spacetime to 
the associated $R$-Minkowski spacetime through the application of these coordinates.

This study introduces an open source Python framework that utilizes background knowledge and observational data for the purpose of inferring causal relationships. This framework is comprised of two main components: a part that applies the concept of ANM models through regression calculations, and another part that employs GCPC under the GCC framework, which requires inputs in the form of interventional distributions. This framework is designed to be scalable, capable of processing up to thousands of variables in parallel, and requires installation of specific libraries including ANTS, Scikit-learn, and multiprocessing. A detailed example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework, and additional details about the underlying theories of ANM and GCPC are available in the cited references.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically focusing on an intermediate speed range where a surface seal forms and shapes the entry process. Existing theoretical models do not effectively explain this regime, thus our research aims to fill this gap. Experimental results, supported by detailed high-speed imaging, allow us to develop a revised theoretical model incorporating a seal. This model leads to key dimensionless parameters, including a Froude number for the seal, and enables prediction of seal stability, pressure distribution, and vertical movement. Validated against a broader dataset, our model successfully captures both the characteristics of the seal regime and transition points to other surface seal models, demonstrating the importance of understanding this phenomenon.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to uncover the range of universal symmetries that may be present. Generalized $\theta$-terms are a key aspect of these theories. We examined how these terms and the superpotential dictate the symmetry-breaking patterns. It was discovered that in order for a universal global symmetry to exist, it is necessary for non-abelian gauge symmetries to be present. We determined the R-charge assignments for the non-abelian gauge fields that would enable these patterns, which in turn led to an exhaustive analysis of Lagrangian charges and an identification of the R-symmetry breaking terms within the EFTs. We discovered that generalized $\theta$-terms often preserve more Lagrangian charges than do the superpotential cubic interactions. As an added observation, we discovered that it is possible to obtain insight into the R-charge assignments by applying 't Hooft anomaly matching conditions to non-abelian chiral symmetries.

Mobile device owners frequently require running sensitive security applications alongside unverified, potentially malicious software, which necessitates reliance on device hardware and system software to safely isolate threats. 

This often leads users to trust the same device hardware and system software that may inherently be compromised by anonymous hackers seeking to phish for secrets or deploy malware. 

We explore the concept of minimizing trust towards device hardware and system software to counter this issue, introducing MinTrust as a novel approach for secure multi-tenancy. 

By utilizing exclusively-used hardware, such as raw NAND and a bare-metal boot loader, and employing only hardware features that require pre-existing isolation, like Intel's Intel SGX, we successfully isolate attacks while allowing interaction with virtualization technologies for malicious apps. 

We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach with an end-to-end case study, successfully deploying a phishing application and malware security app on an Intel-based Android device, and showing that users can trust external storage devices more than they currently trust their mobile device memory.

We investigated the impacts of highly intense noisy perturbations on the gradient algorithm used in policy optimization.
We showed that, due to the $O(1)$-level noise, the algorithm may converge to an incorrect deterministic policy, representing a significant deviation from the optimal policy.
We introduced a robust algorithm based on the median median estimation, capable of addressing strongly noisy perturbations.
We developed a method to determine the sample complexity of the median median estimation algorithm in terms of various environment parameters.
In contrast to existing work dealing with mild noise assumptions, our algorithm ensures sample efficiency with only a constant factor increase, involving a minimal overhead (e.g., seven times) compared to the sample complexity of the standard policy gradient method under noise-free conditions.

We uncover an unselectable version of the box game paradox, featuring players making remarkably accurate predictions of unknown real numbers without access to relevant information. Additionally, our analysis confirms the requirement of choice in solving the classic problem and examines alternative configurations of the game.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as multi-phonon physics, is driving research and development for both fundamental understanding and technological advancements in the areas of metrology, communication, and computing. Despite external and longitudinal magnetic fields being able to influence spins through the interaction with the Zeeman effect, these fields are excluded from the current study, as they significantly restrict the creation of large Rabi oscillillations in dark excitons. Instead, this study focuses on achieving giant Rabi oscillillations in multi-phonon states of dark excitons, caused by the interference between the coupling of phonons and the interaction of Coulomb forces. Detecting these fluctuations is possible through time-dependent photoluminescence. Additionally, this study theoretically shows that different two-phonon states exhibit large split phenomena and that, due to their distinct frequencies, these states can be effectively used to implement quantum bit operations based on interference.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group.  We're examining a herringbone lattice with horizontal and vertical glide symmetries, resulting from two interlocking triangular sublattices shifted along the (110) direction.  Contrary to expectations, our theory posits that Dirac cones emerge at high-symmetry points on the Brillouin zone boundary – specifically at R and M points, without needing inversion or time-reversal symmetry.  Furthermore, we demonstrate that adjusting hopping integrals allows for moving these Dirac points to other locations on the Brillouin zone boundary or even within the zone itself.  Notably, our model allows for achieving Weyl points and an anisotropic electron-hole pocket coexistence by simply modifying the hopping integrals.  This work highlights the potential of theoretical models based on non-symmorphic lattices in facilitating the discovery of exotic phenomena in 2D materials and heterostructures.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine several properties of these states, such as their entanglement, superposition, and anti-bunching characteristics, depending on quantum-optical catalysis. Notably, we generate (spare) Fock states, (Schrödinger's) cat states, and vacuum states in other output channels. We utilize the SWAP operator to investigate the transformation of modes and verify our theoretical predictions through simulations.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the predictive framework. Computational trials have demonstrated that the proposed approach excels in predicting specific chemical properties in polymers, also successfully modeling compounds composed of up to 50 non-hydrogen atoms within a monomeric structure.

This paper presents a unified approach to addressing certain complex optimization challenges. Problems of control, estimation, and system design can be redefined as difficult instances of optimization problems. However, solving such issues often involves applying transcription methods. We explore direct transcription methods, including spatial and temporal discretization, and discuss their role in providing initial guesses, solving problems step-by-step, and enabling efficient solution of less idealized versions of optimization issues. We illustrate direct transcription methods with a specific case study on ventilator sharing during the COVID-19 pandemic, where a single ventilator is used to treat two patients by adjusting the timing of their ventilation.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To compensate for these difficulties, doctors often rely on supplementary information from other imaging techniques, medical histories, and endoscopic findings. Acquiring and combining these sources of information is time-consuming and sometimes produces inconclusive results. In this study, we investigate the potential for a more streamlined clinical approach that solely utilizes CT scans for automatically identifying and outlining tumors in the esophagus with satisfactory precision. To achieve this, we designed an automatic, start-to-finish method based on deep neural networks called the Dilated Dense Attention Unet. This model leverages spatial and channel attention mechanisms in dense blocks to prioritize specific features and regions. It also employs dilated convolutional layers to expand its perceptual range and maintain detailed image information. We gathered a comprehensive dataset of CT scans containing varied types of esophageal tumors and a set of reference images and then assessed our method on this collection. We found our network to be more precise and reliable on multiple metrics including Dice Similarity Coefficient, Hausdorff Distance, and Average Surface Distance. We also verified that our attention mechanisms were effective and demonstrated how our model produces high-quality images of healthy, tumor-affected sections of the esophagus.

The expense associated with drilling offshore wells is significant, necessitating real-time management techniques like geosteering to optimize outcomes. By adjusting a well's trajectory in real-time, geosteering enables drilling operators to keep the well within a target zone for an extended period, thereby maximizing production and minimizing costs. Nevertheless, interpreting logs acquired from adjacent wells poses challenges due to the noise and ambiguity inherent in the data, especially when there is a disparity in measurement dates and technologies. Addressing this issue involves integrating and analyzing multiple log types to generate a reliable track of formation boundaries in real-time. This study aims to refine the speed and reliability of interpreting logs and quantifying the uncertainty to enhance geosteering. An innovative ensemble-based method is proposed to simultaneously model multiple logs and evaluate the uncertainty, allowing for more accurate decisions during the drilling process. This method balances the need for speed associated with deterministic formation boundary estimation adjustments in real-time with the benefits of a more reliable probability distribution obtained through Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and a core extraction technique, extensively used to retrieve text-based information for further analysis. One type of NER, nested NER, focuses on recognizing entities within other entities. Most existing nested NER studies apply linear models, which do not adequately capture the hierarchical nature of nested entities. This work overcomes this limitation by modeling nested entities as an integrated whole and proposing a new parsing algorithm to accurately identify all entities at once. Moreover, to address the lack of corpus-level information in NER, this study introduces features based on corpus statistics, including Point-wise Mutual Information, to enhance model performance and adaptability from sentence-level to corpus-level. Our experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art or near-state-of-the-art results on standard benchmarks and showcase significant improvement in domain adaptation through corpus-level feature integration.

We extend the use of tropical methods to counting in arithmetic problems, such as enumerating objects in higher-dimensional spaces using values from specific algebraic structures, over fields that have been modified to have special values, such as plane quartics with specific tangent properties. We look at curves defined by equations with non-negative values and derive a counting formula for these curves, considering how they are affected by lines that touch the curves at specific points or transform into degenerate forms. This counting formula is done by analyzing the tropical versions of these curves and understanding their behavior under certain conditions. Additionally, we show that certain counts of these curves with specific tangent properties, such as those touched by four lines, can be determined by examining their tropical versions. This connection allows us to establish a link between counting these curves using their algebraic properties and their behavior in modified environments. As a bonus, we provide an approach to counting these curves with four lines that touch the curves.

Research into the location detection of mobile nodes within wireless sensor networks is currently ongoing. We develop and test an innovative RSSI-based location finding method suitable for 802.15.4 (ZigBee) networks. To counteract interference between different technologies operating in the same frequency range, we design and execute a new method for calculating the distance between nodes. The aim of this approach is to minimize the average error in location estimation, and when compared to ideal, interference-free results, we have achieved a level of accuracy of less than half a metre using actual hardware.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, we outline potential future datasets, models, and resources to enhance NLP applications for societal betterment, exemplified through an analysis of code-mixing between English and Hindi but with implications for other language combinations.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visually impaired users' needs and practical description generation feasibility. High-quality reference data could be ideal for system evaluation, yet we should also consider other alternatives.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are notable for their diverse structural forms and unique electronic properties. These properties include semi-conductivity and ferroelectricity, which have potential applications in the development of advanced thin-film capacitors and anti-reflective coatings in solar cells. Previous studies on Ta$_2$O$_5$ have focused primarily on specific synthesis methods and comparisons with other lithium-ion battery materials. In this study, we take a different approach, using first-principles theory to thoroughly investigate all possible low-symmetry crystal structures of Ta$_2$O$_5$. By applying methodological innovations and leveraging modern supercomputer resources, we have identified 54 new crystal phases of Ta$_2$O$_5$, in collaboration with experimental partners. In addition, we have used Monte Carlo simulations to explore the energy landscape of these 54 new phases, in order to pinpoint the most stable, or ground state, crystal structure of Ta$_2$O$_5$. Our findings reveal that the energy minimum of Ta$_2$O$_5$ lies in a high-symmetry region of its energy landscape, in contrast to the typically observed low-symmetry amorphous forms. Furthermore, we have used first-principles theory to examine and predict the mechanical, optical, and mechanical properties of this ground state Ta$_2$O$_5$.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to personal factors, such as information literacy, and social media influences, but ignored a third aspect: the impact of the physical separation of Americans in geographical regions. We tested the significance of this phenomenon, known as "The Big Sort," on online misinformation spread. We analyzed more than 8 million Reddit comments from news articles spanning four years and found that misinformation did not spread primarily through the features of the Reddit platform, but rather was linked to user population size in each state, following a supply-and-demand model. Furthermore, variations in misinformation dissemination were explained by local personality traits and cultural characteristics rather than economic, social, or political conditions. In areas where residents are less diligent in nature, and cultures place little emphasis on adherence to norms, we found increased circulation of all news, including credible sources.

We introduce a groundbreaking, efficient, and user-friendly detection algorithm called HALFADO. HALFADO uses a limited number of human judgments to effectively identify anomalies in real-time, high-frequency data streams. Implementing a precise detection system is crucial for empowering human teams across the digital world by providing reliable decision support. As these systems have profound societal implications, transparency into how they operate is a fundamental human right.

Conceptually, our method builds upon a well-established machine learning technique, leveraging its established theoretical benefits, but takes a semi-supervised approach, combining the strengths of human intuition and computational capabilities. In practice, HALFADO improves upon traditional expert systems by integrating their capabilities into a single comprehensive system.

We showcase the algorithm's performance in two real-world scenarios: (1) half of the judgments from a fully trained anomaly detection system are provided by humans, and the other half by HALFADO; and (2) one quarter of the training data is labeled by humans, with the remaining seven quarters handled by HALFADO.

Our experiments demonstrate that in both real-world scenarios, HALFADO learns to detect anomalies with human-like efficiency in a variety of data streams, outperforming fully trained anomaly detection systems and traditional human-only approaches.

We anticipate that HALFADO will have wide-ranging applications in diverse sectors such as cybersecurity, cybersecurity, and cybersecurity.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, learning from solely observed actions does not take full advantage of audio feedback from the instructor. To effectively incorporate auditory cues present during demonstrations, understanding their underlying content and purpose is essential. This study examines audio input from humans instructing a robot using Sawyer via spoken language by analyzing three key features: speech duration, tone variation, and speech content. Evaluating these features across four dimensions, it was discovered that instructors frequently use the same vocabulary to describe specific task elements despite varying situations such as task types, audio instructions, and errors encountered during demonstrations. However, differences in speech patterns including duration and inflection are present across these conditions, showing that human speech carries significant, potentially valuable information for enhancing robotic learning through demonstration-based methods.

Building on previous work, we propose an algorithm to randomly generate ordered trees of any degree, based on a pre-specified sequence of numbers representing possible node connections. Our method allows for the generation of binary, n-ary trees, or those with various connection patterns. We demonstrate that this algorithm is both accurate and efficient, running in O(n) time with 'n' representing the number of desired nodes. Additionally, we explore potential applications of the algorithm, illustrating its use in deriving formulas by utilizing the underlying proof of correctness.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models and their corresponding Gaussian representations. A promising approach to address this difficulty is through the study of conformal field theories in 1+1 dimensions, specifically focusing on the universal sector of the energy-momentum tensor in this context. A key unifying framework consists of Euler-Arnold equations and their broader integro-differential generalizations, ensuring the well-posedness of state or operator complexity optimization problems. Our comprehensive investigation extends upon prior findings, including the discovery of novel conserved quantities within NIA flows that correspond to novel, physically significant fields. Notably, these quantities enable the derivation of explicit, closed-form solutions for various 2- and 3-point complexity functions. A striking outcome reveals that certain CFT complexity measures can be directly linked to specific correlation function data, such as hadron or particle complexities being proportional to specific quasi-momentum densities.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems and ensure they effectively convey intended information, a robust automated testing framework is urgently needed. We have developed ConversTest, a comprehensive automated testing framework for conversational agents that leverages Python's ChatRebel framework and utilizes Natural Language Generation to create a coherent evaluation environment. ChatRebel isolates the system under test from its underlying data, enabling clearer assessment of the system and its logic. Moreover, ConversTest enables multi-turn dialogue testing and incorporates a mechanism for automated natural language feedback generation through Big-Bench. We have validated the effectiveness of ConversTest by applying it to identify previously unknown bugs in existing applications. In our experiments, we discovered six previously undocumented bugs across three instances. We have also made ConversTest accessible to the research community via an open-source framework and step-by-step instructions via GitHub at https://github.com/wenyu-gh/ConversTest.

Using a sophisticated mathematical model known as the Fisher information matrix, it's possible to estimate the measurement uncertainties and parameter correlations in the Heliocentric Orbital Element (HOLE) parameter space for the eight known planets. The statistical precision with which a hypothetical ninth planet's mass could be determined, given the existing data, is also assessed. Notably, the effect of a ninth planet would most noticeably distort the gravitational influence between Neptune and Pluto. The current measurement errors predominantly randomize the positions of inner planets, rendering their correlation with a ninth planet negligible. Consequently, a ninth planet's mass could potentially be detected through the analysis of gravitational interactions between Neptune and Pluto. Assuming a ninth planet exists beyond Neptune, it would most likely be situated in a stable, low-eccentricity, near-circular orbit between 40-80 AU from the Sun. Under these conditions, a ninth planet between 0.5 to 7 Earth masses could potentially be detected with up to 90% confidence. Notably, the L1 region, previously identified as one of the more stable areas between Neptune and Pluto, falls within this 0.5 to 7 Earth mass range.

Previous studies have demonstrated that Translation Memory (TM) can enhance Neural Machine Translation (NMT) performance. Unlike existing approaches which rely on bilingual corpora for TM and employ source-side similarity searches, our proposed framework leverages monolingual data and retrieves memories in a cross-lingual manner. Notably, our framework offers two significant advantages: firstly, it enables vast amounts of monolingual data to be incorporated into TM; secondly, both the memory retriever and the NMT model can be jointly optimized for translation objectives. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves substantial gains in performance and outperforms TM-augmented NMT baselines even when utilizing bilingual TM. Furthermore, our model's capacity to tap into monolingual data allows it to excel in low-resource and domain adaptation scenarios.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, namely low-variance circles and Hawking points, could provide evidence for the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model. These patterns are predicted to originate from previous black hole mergers and evaporation events. We analyzed the Planck and WMAP data using a machine learning tool called HawkingNet, and initially found potential anomalies resembling low-variance circles and Hawking points. However, these anomalies were later removed, and upon re-examination, we found no statistically significant evidence supporting the existence of low-variance circles or Hawking points. Our analysis does indicate the presence of local non-Gaussian fluctuations in the CMB, suggesting that the real sky may differ from theoretical predictions.

This paper builds upon previous work of the second author with Daskalopoulos and Vazquez, which involved introducing a Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature and demonstrating the existence of mild solutions. The current research expands on that study by establishing the convergence of the flow under certain data conditions within a broader framework. The new results are derived from an approach simplified by Struwe in his book.

To recognize new categories from minimal labeled data, few-shot learning has been rapidly evolving in recent years. However, traditional methods that rely on average operations for calculating prototypes often struggle due to the influence of outliers. This research proposes a new, effective framework that utilizes an episodic prototype generator module to create more representative prototypes from limited support data, reducing the impact of outliers and resulting in preferable models. The framework's ability is further showcased by the substantial improvement it yields over baseline models and the comparable performance it achieves to existing methods on datasets like miniImageNet, tieredImageNet, and cross-domain benchmarks (miniImageNet to CUB-200-2011).

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the pervasive issue of data sparsity in recommender systems. Single-target and dual-target CDR approaches are often hindered by the limitations of requiring at least one well-specified dense domain and overfitting to known user preferences in those dense domains. To tackle these challenges, we introduce a novel framework called Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDCR) that is specifically designed to handle multiple data-sparse domains, by bridting isolated data silos and enhancing user preference understanding across all involved domains. Unlike conventional CDR methods, we view every domain, be it a under-nutried subject area or a cross-disciplinary topic, as a distinct data silo. To address the issue of isolated training, we introduce a Multi-Space Enhanced (MS-E) mechanism to integrate and leverage information from all domains, by incorporating auxiliary information and a knowledge graph, and integrating these elements with loss functions, to achieve effective knowledge transfer and mutual compensation. To address the challenge of user preference diversity, we introduce a Enhanced Comprehensive Aspect Preference (ECAP) mechanism that leverages both local and global information, to model user preferences from multiple perspectives and mitigate preference divergence. The proposed MS-CSR model, which integrates all these innovative components, exhibits superior performance on two real-world datasets in terms of precision, recall, and F-score metrics.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of constraint solver for their boundary. This optimization technique has gained popularity in fields like machine learning, finance, and telecommunications due to its ability to provide scalable and interpretable models. Currently, second-order cone and semidefinite cones are commonly employed, but an expanding list of cones is becoming available through the development of new algorithms. This approach requires the development of tailored interior point methods, barrier functions, and active set algorithms for each cone type. Recent advances have led to the development of hypatia, a comprehensive interior point method solver that leverages an extensive variety of cones and provides a robust framework for machine learning applications. This tool supports over 100 types of convex functions, including some that anticipate future trends in the field.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality control to ensure reliable and efficient analysis, especially for extensive research projects. Several approaches have been explored to develop scalable and dependable quality control pipelines, but effectively generalizing these methods across diverse, previously unseen data remains a significant challenge. This study evaluated the MRIQC pipeline's performance on multiple large datasets, utilizing ABIDE and UK Biobank data. By utilizing multi-class evaluation metrics and increasing classification confidence thresholds, multiple classifiers were assessed for their efficacy. This multi-class evaluation approach yielded improved results compared to the original binary classification framework. Furthermore, incorporating additional data sources enhanced MRIQC's generalizability. Notably, utilizing ABIDE data alone resulted in high precision (0.95) and recall (0.90) scores on UK Biobank data. Conversely, training the same classifier with only 100 subjects from the UK Biobank dataset led to poor generalization (0.55 F1 score) on the remaining data. These findings highlight the importance of employing robust evaluation metrics and sufficient, diverse training data to effectively assess and assess the reliability of automated quality control systems for MRI.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for more advanced solution methods.

Intel's Optane DC Persistent Memory Module (DC PMM) has reached commercial viability as the first commercially available nonvolatile memory DIMM. It offers fast, byte-granular data access similar to DRAM, combined with power-fail safe storage. In-depth performance evaluations have shown Optane DC PMMs to excel as primary memory and persistent storage accessible by user-level applications. Various modes and benchmarks have been used to measure Optane DC PMMs performance under different scenarios, including comparison to DRAM, which revealed that in certain applications, Optane DC PMMs matched DRAM's performance. In other cases, they outperformed DRAM. Furthermore, user-level benchmarks demonstrated the potential of dcrl for diverse workloads without compromising performance.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how this framework can facilitate cooperative behavior between agents that move at varying speeds in an one-dimensional space, resulting in their meeting point. The increased capacity to incorporate inter-agent communication speeds and pairwise preferences into this model is highlighted as a significant advantage that sets it apart from previous work, which generally focuses on agents in motion and their speeds but neglects other critical factors that influence their cooperative decision-making processes. Numerical simulations are employed to validate that this approach converges upon stable, metastic states that reflect agents' precepts, which include global system energy minimization, the impact of agent movement on their surroundings, and their desire to meet in an energy-efficient manner.

We used first-principles calculations to examine the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 (x = 1, 0.5, 1) in this study. Specifically, we focused on the cubic phases of these compounds. By comparing our theoretical results to available experimental data, we found good agreement. Our analysis revealed that both GdSn3 and CmSn3 exhibit a characteristic A7-like band structure. Furthermore, we discovered that both compounds display both itinerant and localized magnetic behavior. Notably, we determined that both GdSn3 and CmSn3 follow the 122-valence electron rule, indicating metavalency. Additionally, our calculations indicated that CmSn3 may exhibit type-A long-period oscillations. Moreover, we found that mixed-site doping of Gd and Cm in Sn3 could strengthen the 4f electron interactions, resulting in enhanced magnetic moments.

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the fundamental symmetry group from $SU(2) \times U(1)$ to $SU(3)\times U(1)$, while assigning the three fermion families in a non-consecutive manner. In contrast to the bilepton model, many more particles are expected to be observed at an energy scale of a few TeV, aligning with the design parameters of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). However, the theory also predicts a lower value for the cosmological dark matter density than currently estimated. Consequently, certain mechanisms must be implemented to supplement dark matter density predictions. The article then outlines potential methods for testing this model, including identifying new gauge bosons, scalar particles, and a type of dark matter candidate known as weakly interacting massive particles.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Shwartz established a significant link between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. Our study extends this connection to the finite classical Coxeter group Bn by standardizing the ordered generating sequences, which allows us to identify exchange laws for Bn. Moreover, we establish a connection between the standard ordered generating sequences, Coxeter length, and the descent set of Bn.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate weak lensing convergence by combining data on the positions and photometry of foreground galaxies. A correlation between this approach and the residual Hubble diagram values of Type Ia supernovae holds a $3.6\sigma$ significance and is consistent with dark matter effects due to galactic halos. Furthermore, we constrained galactic halo properties, including the mass-to-light ratio $\Gamma$ and the radial distribution of matter density within haloes $\rho(r)$. Based on this analysis, we formulated an equation to calculate the lensing convergence $\kappa$. If applied to the 450 SN Ia in the Pantheon-plus dataset, this approach is projected to provide a $1.6\sigma$ test of General Relativity's validity on cosmological scales. Additionally, it may offer $1.1\sigma$ constraints on galaxy halo parameters $\Gamma$ and $\rho(r)$.

These are lecture notes for a 6-hour mini-course on stochastic partial differential equations presented at the University of Oxford in April-May 2021. 

The main objective of these lecture notes is to provide an in-depth explanation of the variational method for monotone and coercive stochastic partial differential equations. 

The necessary background on the functional analytic framework along with the properties of the operator generating the heat semigroup in both $L^2$- and Gelfand triple settings are also covered. 

The core material includes the proof of the variationals parabolic equation theory and the establishment of the uniqueness result for the associated random variational elliptic equation. 

The lectures also include references to other topics that could be covered in a more comprehensive treatment of this subject.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on reliable solid-state sources of photons that are linked together. A reliable method for creating T-type defects in silicon wafers has been elusive until now, as traditional approaches using diamond materials cannot be applied to the high-quality silicon layers found in silicon-on-insulator wafers. In this research, a novel process was demonstrated that allows for precise control of T-type defects in silicon T-centers by first doping the buried oxide layer with a specific type of impurity and then applying an electric field during manufacturing. In addition, a new method for measuring and characterizing these T-type defects based on their interaction with photons has been developed. A model explaining the formation of these T-type defects has also been created, allowing for identification of a highly efficient production process that significantly improves yield.

MRI technology utilizes radio waves to scan the human body and obtain precise, pain-free diagnostic images. These images enable radiologists to visually assess anatomy and physiological processes within the body, ultimately facilitating early disease diagnosis and treatment. Advanced imaging capabilities, combined with sophisticated processing techniques, enable detection of hard-to-spot tumors. This assignment delves into Automated Tumor Detection by comparing conventional image processing methods, such as morphological analysis and regional growth algorithms, in order to explore their application and effectiveness.

In this research, we explore the properties of a novel algebraic variant of the degenerate Bernoulli polynomial $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$, as well as its corresponding degenerate Bernoulli number. This investigation is grounded in an innovative algebraic framework for generating functions and symbolic evaluation functions, allowing us to derive $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$. Our findings demonstrate intriguing connections with circulant matrices and Galois fields, while showcasing the potential for $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ to be applied in computationally efficient contexts.

The high activity levels of M dwarfs significantly hinder our ability to study their habitable zones due to stellar activity masking planetary signals. This research explores the use of highly active M dwarfs to search for habitable planets in the future, and currently employed activity proxies being effective at localising these potentially promising regions. Two experiments were conducted to examine the impact of line lists selected for least-squares deconvolution (LSD) on the stellar activity signals in radial velocity (LRV) and in relative activity indices (RAI). By comparing the activity signals induced by an LSD constructed from randomly chosen lines versus a parametrically defined one, we found that lines with stronger equivalent widths yield more reproducible RAI signals. This implies that currently used single RAIs, such as those at 6869 Å and 7049 Å, may not be suitable for the detection of Earth-like planets around active M dwarfs, and that multiple, uncorrelated activity indices should instead be used to minimise the risk of mislabelling stars. Furthermore, we outline the procedure for generating line lists for LSD in a manner that optimises the stability of the resulting LRV and RAI signals, and propose testing multiple LSD-constructed line lists to statistically assess the detection of extraterrestrial signals.

This research paper proposes a pair of methods for designing a flexible and efficient data collection process in Wireless Sensor Networks, ensuring high reliability and performance. Firstly, a link quality estimation technique is utilized, enabling swift computation of link quality between nodes. Secondly, a hierarchical sector-based system is established to organize and coordinate nodes within each sector to minimize interference and improve data transmission. The effectiveness of these methods was demonstrated through a protocol, called HBCP, developed and evaluated in a simulated environment utilizing TinyOS and TelosB devices. The outcome of the evaluation revealed that HBCP can achieve very high reliability levels, particularly in large-scale networks and networks prone to bottlenecks.

For our task that considers context, a suitable object detector is needed.
Different object detectors exploit scene context for recognition in varying ways.
This study categorizes object detectors into 3 groups based on context usage:
one that doesn't use context by isolating the input, another that uses partial
context by isolating part of the feature map, and one that uses full context
without isolation.
Our evaluation method assesses the effect of context for each deep detector
category systematically. A specially designed dataset is created to test the
effect of context for deep detectors. The impact of removing the background
context and foreground objects on the MS COCO is also examined.
It is shown that both two-stage and single-stage object detectors can make use
of the context due to their extensive receptive field.
Thus, selecting the best object detector for a particular application depends
on the specific context in question.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations, which involves a given, non-positive function and a unique, bounded Bessel potential, categorized by an infinite growth parameter. The primary aim is established through the application of a compactness principle for admissible functions, originally demonstrated by Sohrbhi and Van Gheluwe, in conjunction with a genus-based method. Furthermore, the study extends its investigation to an analogous dynamic system, which can be found in the associated reference.

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors whose entries reside in the discrete cube, subject to weak admissibility and negative association constraints, yielding substantial improvements of existing upper bounds through a factor of $1/\sqrt{2}$ for sub-Gaussian, Lipschitz, and Hamiltonian functions. This work further develops an alternative method to establish moment inequalities, with direct implications for Hamiltonian and Lipschitz functions under pairwise independence, completely mutual independence, and random curve scenarios, culminating in an upper bound for the expected absolute deviation from the median, derived from mean inequality reasoning.

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic greater than two, and consider the ring of power series $R$ over the Witt vectors of $k$, expanded in variables $t_1, \dots, t_d$. The main aim of this study is to generalize classical Fontaine-Messing theory to a base ring of the form $R$. Notably, we establish theorems enabling the comparison of crystalline and \'etale cohomologies with torsion coefficients for smooth schemes $X$ over $R$.

We investigate the sign change in the difference of dihadron production rates during semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering when the incoming quark's longitudinal spin flips, specifically comparing $g_1$-induced and duality-violating contributions. This analysis helps evaluate the validity of the quark-diquark duality. Using a twist-2 hadron distribution function and a resonance model, we calculate these contributions to demonstrate how they affect the $g_1$-induced and total cos$\phi_S$ asymmetries of dihadron production as the hadron transverse momentum varies. Our results indicate quark-diquark duality holds for certain $x_B$ values but fails elsewhere. Notably, we find that the duality between the cos$\phi_R$ asymmetries driven by $g_1$ and the total asymmetries holds at particular $x_B$ values but not others.

We've established recently, much like our work on Conformal Cyclic Cosmology, that Fock's hypothesized connection between distant galaxies and subatomic particles is aligned with the principles of modern physics, specifically general relativity and the Standard Model.  Inspired by Georges Lemaître's belief in de Sitter space as both beginning and end point of his 'primeval atom' theory, we examine how Fock may have been trying to convey a dual nature of spacetime - having boundaries at infinite distances and temperatures, yet also at zero temperatures - in his writings. We explore Fock's ideas in detail and refer to his relevant passages in these texts.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

This paper presents a Wikipedia-based entity recommendation framework that utilizes an embedding approach, where the Wikipedia database is hierarchically divided into layered graphs to extract entity features and learn entity representations. By combining the extracted information with a lightweight ranking method, this framework effectively suggests related entities to users on Wikipedia. We evaluate our approach through both offline and real-world online tests, demonstrating that our embeddings and recommendations exhibit desirable quality and user engagement. Furthermore, this framework delivers entity recommendations in both English and non-English languages for the Yahoo! Knowledge Graph, where Wikipedia constitutes a fundamental subset.

A key obstacle in kidney transplants arises from the incompatibility between donors and patients, which has been exacerbated by the growing scarcity of kidney donors. Desensitization techniques were developed to overcome the immunological difficulties. Patients receiving incompatible transplants face a higher risk of transplant rejection, infections, and cancer, and are more likely to lose their transplants. We aim at finding the optimal acceptance strategy for incompatible kidneys to maximize societal welfare. A mathematical model taking into account the dynamics of kidney availability, the desensitization techniques' effects, and medical costs was created, which led to an optimal control solution via stochastic differential equations. Key insights gained from sensitivity analysis guided the development of an efficient numerical algorithm for solving the model.

Implicit copulas are the primary choice for analyzing dependencies in complex scenarios due to their ability to effectively model dependence in high-dimensional spaces. The text presents a comprehensive overview of this broad category, encompassing copulas such as elliptical, skew t, factor, time series, and regression copulas, highlighting their key characteristics and applications. The discussion explains how the auxiliary representation of implicit copulas facilitates scalability and usability in statistical modeling, addressing concerns like parameter estimation, likelihood calculation, and model parsimony. The text also covers Bayesian estimation techniques for implicit copulas and the benefits of employing these models in conjunction with time series and regression models, which are the subject of current research advancements. The advantages of using implicit copulas are further illustrated through the examination of econometric applications, including analyses of macroeconomic time series and financial asset pricing.

This paper undertakes a comprehensive mathematical and statistical examination of the word embeddings used in 17,000 financial reports identified as having positive or negative sentiments by the Loughran-McDonald sentiment dictionary.
